en.greeting: Hi! Today we learn how to say 'ada' in English: there is and there are. You'll describe rooms and places, ask what's there and use some and any. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: There is, there are
steps.text: Let's start with the English for 'ada'.
steps.body: For one thing, say **there is** (short: **there's**). For two or more, say **there are**. Then add the place: *There is a bed in my room.* For *tidak ada*, say **there isn't a …**. Don't use **have** for *ada*: 'In my room have a bed' is wrong.

steps.title: Around the house
steps.text: Here are some sentences about rooms and places. Look at is and are.
steps.body: Count first: **one** thing → **is**, **two or more** → **are**. The place usually comes at the end.

examples.en: There is a bed in my room.
There's a big TV in the living room.
examples.id: Ada TV besar di ruang tamu.

examples.en: There are two bathrooms in our house.
examples.id: Ada dua kamar mandi di rumah kami.

examples.en: There are 30 students in my class.
There isn't a wardrobe in my kos room.
examples.id: Tidak ada lemari pakaian di kamar kosku.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Count the tables first.

question.prompt: Pak Hasan's warung is very small. Complete: There ___ only one table.
question.explanation: One table = one thing, so **there is**. **Are** is for two or more, and we don't use **has** for 'ada'.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Now describe a room. Remember: there + is/are + thing + place.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Ada kipas angin di kamarku.
question.solution: There is a fan in my room.
question.explanation: Start with **There is** (one fan), then the thing, then the place: **There is a fan in my room.** Not 'In my room have a fan'.

steps.title: Is there …? Are there …?
steps.text: Now let's ask what is in a place. Very useful when you travel!
steps.body: Put **is** or **are** first: **Is there a …?** (one thing), **Are there …?** (two or more). Answer short with **there**: **Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.** **Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.** Not 'Yes, it is' or 'Yes, have'.

steps.title: Listen and reply
steps.text: Your friend asks you a question. Press play and listen.

question.prompt: Listen to your friend's question. The answer is yes. Choose the short answer.
question.listen: Is there a mosque near your office?
question.explanation: The question starts with **Is there** (one mosque), so the answer is **Yes, there is.** Don't answer with **it**.

steps.title: some and any
steps.text: Last part: two small words for two or more things.
steps.body: Use **some** (= beberapa) in positive sentences: *There are some shops.* Use **any** in negatives and questions: *There aren't any shops.* *Are there any shops?* So 'Are there some shops near here?' is a common mistake. With one thing, use **a/an**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: It's late at night. Which sentence is right?

question.prompt: It's 11 p.m. at the bus station in Jakarta. Which sentence is correct?
options: There aren't some buses to Bogor now.
There are any buses to Bogor now.
There aren't any buses to Bogor now.
question.explanation: It's a negative sentence with **aren't**, so use **any**: **There aren't any buses to Bogor now.** **Some** is for positive sentences, and **any** doesn't go in a positive sentence.

steps.title: Build the question
steps.text: You're hungry and you're near the station. Ask a question.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Ada restoran di dekat stasiun?
question.solution: Are there any restaurants near the station?
question.explanation: Restaurants = two or more, so **Are there**. In a question, use **any**: **Are there any restaurants near the station?**

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards. Say the meaning before you check.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Use it when you describe a room or ask about a place.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · There is / there are
artifact.intro: One thing → is. Two or more → are.
rows: There are two beds. / There are some beds.
tips: Don't use **have** for *ada*: **There is a bed in my room.**
Count first: **There are two chairs**, not 'There is two chairs'.
Questions and negatives take **any**: **Are there any shops near here?**

examples.en: There is a bed in my room.
There are some nice beaches in Lombok.
examples.id: Ada beberapa pantai yang bagus di Lombok.

examples.en: Is there an ATM near here? — Yes, there is.
examples.id: Ada ATM di dekat sini? — Ya, ada.

examples.en: Are there any shops near here?

steps.text: Want more? Watch a short video and try the online tests.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita belajar cara bilang 'ada' dalam bahasa Inggris: there is dan there are. Kamu akan mendeskripsikan ruangan dan tempat, menanyakan apa yang ada, dan memakai some dan any. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: There is, there are
steps.text: Kita mulai dari bahasa Inggrisnya 'ada'.
steps.body: Untuk satu benda, ucapkan **there is** (pendeknya: **there's**). Untuk dua atau lebih, ucapkan **there are**. Lalu tambahkan tempatnya: *There is a bed in my room.* Untuk *tidak ada*, ucapkan **there isn't a …**. Jangan pakai **have** untuk *ada*: 'In my room have a bed' salah.

steps.title: Di sekitar rumah
steps.text: Ini beberapa kalimat tentang ruangan dan tempat. Perhatikan is dan are.
steps.body: Hitung dulu: **satu** benda → **is**, **dua atau lebih** → **are**. Tempatnya biasanya di akhir kalimat.

examples.en: There is a bed in my room.
There's a big TV in the living room.
examples.id: Ada TV besar di ruang tamu.

examples.en: There are two bathrooms in our house.
examples.id: Ada dua kamar mandi di rumah kami.

examples.en: There are 30 students in my class.
There isn't a wardrobe in my kos room.
examples.id: Tidak ada lemari pakaian di kamar kosku.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Hitung dulu mejanya.

question.prompt: Warung Pak Hasan sangat kecil. Lengkapi: There ___ only one table.
question.explanation: One table = satu benda, jadi **there is**. **Are** untuk dua atau lebih, dan kita tidak memakai **has** untuk 'ada'.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sekarang deskripsikan sebuah kamar. Ingat: there + is/are + benda + tempat.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Ada kipas angin di kamarku.
question.solution: There is a fan in my room.
question.explanation: Mulai dengan **There is** (satu kipas), lalu bendanya, lalu tempatnya: **There is a fan in my room.** Bukan 'In my room have a fan'.

steps.title: Is there …? Are there …?
steps.text: Sekarang kita bertanya apa yang ada di suatu tempat. Sangat berguna saat bepergian!
steps.body: Taruh **is** atau **are** di depan: **Is there a …?** (satu benda), **Are there …?** (dua atau lebih). Jawab singkat dengan **there**: **Yes, there is. / No, there isn't.** **Yes, there are. / No, there aren't.** Bukan 'Yes, it is' atau 'Yes, have'.

steps.title: Dengar dan jawab
steps.text: Temanmu bertanya sesuatu. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.prompt: Dengarkan pertanyaan temanmu. Jawabannya ya. Pilih jawaban singkatnya.
question.listen: Is there a mosque near your office?
question.explanation: Pertanyaannya dimulai dengan **Is there** (satu masjid), jadi jawabannya **Yes, there is.** Jangan jawab dengan **it**.

steps.title: some dan any
steps.text: Bagian terakhir: dua kata kecil untuk dua benda atau lebih.
steps.body: Pakai **some** (= beberapa) dalam kalimat positif: *There are some shops.* Pakai **any** dalam kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan: *There aren't any shops.* *Are there any shops?* Jadi 'Are there some shops near here?' adalah kesalahan yang umum. Untuk satu benda, pakai **a/an**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sudah larut malam. Kalimat mana yang benar?

question.prompt: Jam 11 malam di terminal bus di Jakarta. Kalimat mana yang benar?
options: There aren't some buses to Bogor now.
There are any buses to Bogor now.
There aren't any buses to Bogor now.
question.explanation: Ini kalimat negatif dengan **aren't**, jadi pakai **any**: **There aren't any buses to Bogor now.** **Some** untuk kalimat positif, dan **any** tidak dipakai dalam kalimat positif.

steps.title: Susun pertanyaannya
steps.text: Kamu lapar dan sedang di dekat stasiun. Ajukan pertanyaan.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Ada restoran di dekat stasiun?
question.solution: Are there any restaurants near the station?
question.explanation: Restaurants = dua atau lebih, jadi **Are there**. Dalam pertanyaan, pakai **any**: **Are there any restaurants near the station?**

steps.title: Ulangan cepat
steps.text: Balik kartunya. Sebutkan artinya sebelum kamu cek.

steps.title: Contekan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Pakai saat kamu mendeskripsikan ruangan atau bertanya tentang suatu tempat.

artifact.title: Contekan · There is / there are
artifact.intro: Satu benda → is. Dua atau lebih → are.
rows: There are two beds. / There are some beds.
tips: Jangan pakai **have** untuk *ada*: **There is a bed in my room.**
Hitung dulu: **There are two chairs**, bukan 'There is two chairs'.
Pertanyaan dan kalimat negatif memakai **any**: **Are there any shops near here?**

examples.en: There is a bed in my room.
There are some nice beaches in Lombok.
examples.id: Ada beberapa pantai yang bagus di Lombok.

examples.en: Is there an ATM near here? — Yes, there is.
examples.id: Ada ATM di dekat sini? — Ya, ada.
